name: Splink
title: Splink
description: How likely a name is each of a few held records, scored by Splink with fixed weights: the same names always give the same scores, with no model call
whenToUse: Dedupe a name read from a document against the records already held: the name and each candidate's names in, a probability per candidate out, from Splink's own matching model (Fellegi-Sunter, comparing the name's core by spelling and its place, role and legal form apart). Use it in front of a judge: a score near one links, near zero rules out, and only what falls between goes to a model. It runs on the platform's document service, wherever that is hosted, and reads and writes nothing: the caller holds the records and decides.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: { name, candidates: [{ id, names: [..] }] }: the name read, and each held record's names

outputs.name: scores
outputs.description: One per candidate, best first: { id, probability, best }, where best is the candidate's name that scored highest

input.title: Name and candidates
input.description: As JSON: { "name": "...", "candidates": [{ "id": "r1", "names": ["...", "..."] }] }. Usually set by the caller (an object's matching), e.g. return { name, candidates }

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: documents
package.packageFile:
# DOCUMENTS — the platform's own document service (services/documents, a Python service beside
# umap): a file in, its structure out. Text in reading order, every table as rows, every figure
# as an image with its caption, every ordered list, the dates a document carries, and where on
# which page each sits. docs/unoverse/data/documents/README.md.
#
# ONE DOOR, ONE NODE: ParseDocument, RenderDocument, InventoryFolder, ReadCover, ReadValues, Splink. Each but Splink (one name against a few, answered at once) is a JOB on
# the service (start, poll, collect), which is the LlamaParse shape, so the poll capability does
# the waiting. A door does one job, so one can be improved or replaced without touching what
# calls it: a census before reading, a cover before filing, a parse when the whole is wanted.
#
# THE HOST IS THE ENGINE, at loopback (`scope.engineUrl`, :4101), which forwards to the service
# (routes/documents.ts) the way it reaches umap. A node's call must be https or loopback
# (allowedHosts.ts refuses a plaintext request to any other host), and a compose service on the
# Docker network is neither; the engine holds the service's address so no node and no file does.

name: documents
displayName: Documents
description: >-
  Read a file into its structure with the platform's document service. Text, tables as rows,
  figures, lists, dates, provenance
version: 0.1.0
category: ingest
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

features:
  - Parse PDF, Word, slides, spreadsheets, HTML and images into one typed structure
  - Tables as rows with units parsed, figures as images, ordered lists as steps
  - Render any page or region as an image
  - "Inventory a folder: kinds, pages, dates, duplicates"
  - "Read a cover: what each file is about and the date it states, from named cells, no model"
  - "Read values: the figures a parsed document stated, refused whole when they do not add up to what it says about itself"
  - "Splink: how likely a name is each of a few held records, scored the same way every time, no model call"

allowedHosts:
  # LOOPBACK ONLY, numeric form (the pattern rejects a bare "localhost"): every call goes to the
  # engine's own listener, which forwards to the service. No third-party host, ever.
  - 127.0.0.1

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  transport: [json]
  # Every door is a job: without `poll` an executor would settle on the receipt and emit the job
  # id as the answer.
  poll: true

files.api/run.yaml:
# THE SCORES, from the engine at loopback (package.yaml says why), which forwards to the documents
# service's /splink. Not a job: one name against a few candidates answers at once.

- name: score
  method: POST
  url: "return scope.engineUrl + '/documents/splink'"
  transport: json

  body:
    name: >-
      return (() => { const raw = config.input; const v = raw && typeof raw === 'object' ? raw : (String(raw || '').trim() ? JSON.parse(String(raw)) : {}); return String(v.name || ''); })()
    candidates: >-
      return (() => { const raw = config.input; const v = raw && typeof raw === 'object' ? raw : (String(raw || '').trim() ? JSON.parse(String(raw)) : {}); return Array.isArray(v.candidates) ? v.candidates : []; })()

  timeoutMs: 30000

  error:
    when: "return !!response.detail || !!response.error"
    message: "return response.error || (typeof response.detail === 'string' ? response.detail : JSON.stringify(response.detail))"
files.config.yaml:
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [input]
  properties:
    input:
      type: string
      title: Name and candidates
      description: >-
        As JSON: { "name": "...", "candidates": [{ "id": "r1", "names": ["...", "..."] }] }. Usually
        set by the caller (an object's matching), e.g. return { name, candidates }
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
"ui:order": [input]
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  - name: input
    type: object
    description: "{ name, candidates: [{ id, names: [..] }] }: the name read, and each held record's names"
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: scores
    type: array
    description: "One per candidate, best first: { id, probability, best }, where best is the candidate's name that scored highest"

credentials: []
files.node.yaml:
type: Splink
kind: PromiseNode

name: Splink
category: Documents
color: "#0F766E"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

description: >-
  How likely a name is each of a few held records, scored by Splink with fixed weights: the
  same names always give the same scores, with no model call

whenToUse: >-
  Dedupe a name read from a document against the records already held: the name and each
  candidate's names in, a probability per candidate out, from Splink's own matching model
  (Fellegi-Sunter, comparing the name's core by spelling and its place, role and legal form
  apart). Use it in front of a judge: a score near one links, near zero rules out, and only what
  falls between goes to a model. It runs on the platform's document service, wherever that is
  hosted, and reads and writes nothing: the caller holds the records and decides.

auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # A pure function of its inputs: the same name and candidates always score the same. Remembered
  # under the documents service's own version, so a change to how names are compared forgets them.
  cacheable:
    answeredBy: documents
files.test.yaml:
# THE NODE UNDER GUARD, against the real service. Made-up names: the same firm spelled two ways,
# and another firm. Asserted on order and range, never on an exact probability.
testData:
  config:
    input: '{"name":"Example Capital Management Ltd","candidates":[{"id":"r1","names":["Example Capital Management Limited"]},{"id":"r2","names":["Market Holdings Inc."]}]}'
  inputs: {}
  expect:
    # The same firm scores near one and first; another firm scores low.
    scores: >-
      return output.scores.length === 2 && output.scores[0].id === 'r1'
        && output.scores[0].probability > 0.9 && output.scores[1].probability < 0.1
